minutes.headline: Selectmen deferred the Conservation Commission conflict exemption to Jan 12, asking for data on affected residents.
minutes.summary: The board discussed the school building committee's possible use of contingency money for add-ons outside the original scope. The town manager said bond counsel's written opinion is coming. It reviewed the Conservation Commission's outline and put the conflict-of-interest exemption vote off to January 12, pending data on how many residents are affected. It also approved a tollbooth fundraiser, license renewals, a county selectmen's association membership and two DPW appointments.

what_happened.line: The Select Board put off its vote on the Conservation Commission's conflict-of-interest exemption until January 12 and asked for data on how many residents are affected.
The board discussed the school building committee's possible use of contingency money for add-ons outside the original scope; the town manager said bond counsel's written opinion is coming.
The board favored inviting the school building committee to a joint workshop after the bond counsel opinion, rather than sending a letter.
Motions were made on a tollbooth fundraiser, license renewals, a county selectmen's association seat and two DPW appointments; the minutes record no audible results.
There will be no December 22 meeting; the next meeting is January 5.

why_it_matters: School building contingency money is a pool the town may be asked to spend on items the state will not reimburse, so any use of it falls on the town budget, mostly taxes, at a time when projected deficits were raised.
The Conservation Commission exemption is still undecided, so how it applies to affected residents will not be settled until the January 12 vote.
watch_next: January 12: the Select Board's vote on the Conservation Commission conflict-of-interest exemption.
Bond counsel's written opinion on the school building contingency, and a possible joint workshop with the school building committee.
